publication: The Newark Herald (pp. 1-12) bound with New Jersey Herald News (pp. 13-20)
summary: Two separate Newark Black weeklies bound together in one scan, both for the week ending Saturday, July 23, 1938. Pages 1-12 are The Newark Herald, Vol. 11, No. 23, City Edition. Pages 13-20 are the New Jersey Herald News, Vol. 1, No. 12, whose own front page leads with 'RACE BAN CLOSES POOL' and the banner 'Winge, Interviewed In Jail, Bares Melodrama Of His Flight In Car With Black Bag of Gold By His Side'. The Newark Herald front page covers the NJ State Federation of Colored Women's Clubs convention in Bordentown, the Daniel E. Winge embezzlement sentencing (sentenced Wednesday, July 20, by Judge Daniel J. Brennen), an Englewood housing-conditions expose by Dr. William F. Willoughby, and the North Jersey Baptist Association Silver Jubilee convention with extensive delegate lists. Page 4 and page 13 carry the Elizabeth Dowd Natatorium pool race ban and the drowning of William 'Bud' Jackson, 17, in the Staten Island Sound within 600 feet of the pool from which he was barred. Other major stories: the American Woodmen regional conference in Newark; NAACP special counsel Charles H. Houston's resignation; and US Attorney General Homer Cummings' inaction on lynchings in Rolling Fork, Mississippi and Arab, Georgia. Sports pages cover Newark Eagles Negro National League baseball and boxing news around John Henry Lewis and Tony Galento. Entertainment pages cover the Apollo Theatre, the film 'The Duke Is Tops' (Ralph Cooper, Lena Horne), a reprinted Paul Robeson speech, and nightlife/society columns ('Mainly About Tan Town,' 'Sophisticates,' 'The New Jersey Whirl Uncensored'). Extensive local community correspondent columns cover Montclair, East Orange, Bayonne, Summit, Hackensack, Vaux Hall, Long Branch, and other NJ towns with club meetings, weddings, church notices, and social notes naming dozens of residents.

Englewood housing-conditions expose by Dr. William F. Willoughby

Newark Eagles doubleheader vs Philadelphia Stars, Ruppert Stadium

connections: This scan binds two distinct Newark Black weeklies: The Newark Herald (Vol. 11, No. 23, pp. 1-12) and the New Jersey Herald News (Vol. 1, No. 12, pp. 13-20). The two papers were competitors publishing the same week, not one title. Attribute items by page: pp. 1-12 to the Newark Herald, pp. 13-20 to the New Jersey Herald News.
Names Black-press-adjacent figures (Julius J. Adams, Lou Blackmon, Charles Countee Edwards, Dewey Ackis, Samuel Russell III) as staff columnists appearing in this bundle.
References the Negro Actors' Guild of America newsletter edited by Mrs. Geraldine Dismond.
Reports on the American Woodmen and NAACP, national Black civic/fraternal organizations with NJ chapters.
